objectives: Use the definite plural for specific things and people.
Choose the object pronoun (mig, dig, honom, henne, oss, er, dem) by its role, not its place in the sentence.

Invite someone, or say no kindly and suggest another day.

teacherNote.title: Invite someone and agree a date
teacherNote.body: Lesson 11 in one cinema plan: “the” in plural (biljetterna), me, you, him and her (mig, dig, henne), dates (den tjugofjärde maj) and a kind no with a new idea. As you listen, notice who does each action and who receives it.

speakers.name: Maja

speakers.name: Alex
speakers.fi: Ja, gärna! När vill du gå?

chunks.label: ANOTHER DAY

recall.prompt: When do Maja and Alex go to the cinema?
recall.explanation: Den tjugofjärde maj. Det är en söndag.

recall.prompt: Why can Elin not come on the twenty-fourth?

dialogue.speaker: Maja
dialogue.fi: Hej Alex! Vill du gå på bio med mig?
dialogue.en: Hi Alex! Do you want to go to the cinema with me?

dialogue.speaker: Alex
dialogue.fi: Ja, gärna! När vill du gå?
dialogue.en: Yes, gladly! When do you want to go?

dialogue.speaker: Maja
dialogue.fi: Den tjugofjärde maj. Det är en söndag. Filmen börjar klockan sju.
dialogue.en: On the twenty-fourth of May. It is a Sunday. The film starts at seven.

dialogue.speaker: Alex
dialogue.fi: Bra. Ska vi fråga Elin också? Jag ringer henne nu.
dialogue.en: Good. Shall we ask Elin too? I will call her now.

dialogue.speaker: Alex
dialogue.fi: Hej Elin! Vill du följa med oss på bio den tjugofjärde?
dialogue.en: Hi Elin! Do you want to come to the cinema with us on the twenty-fourth?

dialogue.speaker: Elin
dialogue.fi: Tack för inbjudan! Tyvärr kan jag inte då. Jag ska träffa mina föräldrar.
dialogue.en: Thanks for the invitation! Unfortunately I cannot then. I am meeting my parents.

dialogue.speaker: Elin
dialogue.fi: Men kan ni gå den tjugotredje i stället?
dialogue.en: But can you go on the twenty-third instead?

dialogue.speaker: Alex
dialogue.en: Maja, does the twenty-third suit you?

dialogue.speaker: Maja
dialogue.fi: Tyvärr inte. På lördagar jobbar jag på kaféet.
dialogue.en: Unfortunately not. On Saturdays I work at the café.

dialogue.speaker: Elin
dialogue.fi: Synd! Då följer jag med nästa gång. Ha det så kul!
dialogue.en: What a pity! Then I will come along next time. Have fun!

dialogue.speaker: Alex
dialogue.fi: Tack! Vi berättar allt för dig sedan.
dialogue.en: Thanks! We will tell you everything afterwards.

dialogue.speaker: Maja
dialogue.fi: Jag köper biljetterna i kväll och skickar dem till dig, Alex. Vi ses framför bion kvart i sju!
dialogue.en: I will buy the tickets tonight and send them to you, Alex. See you in front of the cinema at quarter to seven!

pages.title: Textbook page practice: Skvaller
pages.intro: Red words on this page come in pairs: first the plural (löparskor), then “the” plural (löparskorna). Notice which ending each one takes.
recallCues: Describe the running shoes, toy cars and discounted figures.
Thank Maria, discuss prices and ask about the messages.
Explain the old models, then acknowledge the messages.
Say where the children are and ask for the news.
Start to say who she is.

lines.speaker: Berättare
lines.fi: Maria visar vad hon köpte när hon var ute med Nora.
lines.en: Maria shows what she bought when she was out with Nora.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.fi: Jag köpte nya löparskor till dig eftersom du måste motionera lite mer. Till Jonas köpte jag leksaksbilar för 99 euro. Nils fick två nya figurer som var på rea med 50% rabatt.
lines.en: I bought new running shoes for you because you need to exercise a little more. For Jonas I bought toy cars for 99 euros. Nils got two new figures that were on sale with a 50% discount.

lines.speaker: Peter
lines.fi: Löparskorna är jättefina, tack så mycket! De passar mig perfekt. Men leksaksbilarna var lite dyra... Varför var figurerna på rea? Förresten, fick du mina meddelanden om Andreas?
lines.en: The running shoes are lovely, thank you very much! They fit me perfectly. But the toy cars were a little expensive... Why were the figures on sale? By the way, did you get my messages about Andreas?

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.fi: De är gamla modeller så de var billigare. Det fanns många barn som ville ha dem. Ja, jag fick meddelandena och jag känner hans älskarinna.
lines.en: They are old models, so they were cheaper. There were many children who wanted them. Yes, I got the messages, and I know his mistress.

lines.speaker: Peter
lines.fi: Nähä! Barnen leker ute just nu, berätta!
lines.en: No way! The children are playing outside right now. Tell me!

naturalNotes.note: Bestämd form means “the” form. Look at the last letter of the plural: -r → add -na, -n → add -a, no ending → add -en.

naturalNotes.source: Det fanns många barn som ville ha dem.
naturalNotes.note: Dem here means the figures. The simpler sentence says the same thing.

hunt.instructions: Tap each bold red “the” form. The note tells you which ending it took and why.
hunt.missHint: Look for the bold red words: the “the” plural forms.

spots.rule: the running shoes. Plural löparskor ends in -r, so add -na.
the toy cars. Plural leksaksbilar ends in -r, so add -na.
the figures. Plural figurer ends in -r, so add -na.
the messages. Plural meddelanden already ends in -n, so add only -a.
the children. Plural barn has no ending, so add -en.

pages.title: Textbook page practice: Vill du gå på bio med mig?
pages.intro: Follow who hears, tells, messages and waits for whom.
pages.imageAlt: Textbook page 34, Vill du gå på bio med mig?
recallCues: Call Sofia, tell her to hurry and mention the taxi.

Offer to call Peter about being late.

Point out Peter and Sara waiting.

lines.speaker: Ingrid
lines.fi: Sofia, hör du mig? Skynda dig! En taxi väntar på oss!
lines.en: Sofia, can you hear me? Hurry up! A taxi is waiting for us!

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.fi: Förlåt mamma! Jag är klar om 5 minuter.
lines.en: Sorry, Mum. I will be ready in five minutes.

lines.speaker: Ingrid
lines.fi: Jag ska ringa Peter och berätta för honom att vi blir lite sena.
lines.en: I will call Peter and tell him that we will be a little late.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.fi: Tack! Jag messade Sara, jag har inte tid att ringa henne nu.
lines.en: Thanks! I messaged Sara; I do not have time to call her now.

lines.speaker: Berättare
lines.en: A little later, in front of the cinema.

lines.speaker: Ingrid
lines.fi: Jag ser dem! Där står Peter och Sara och väntar.
lines.en: I see them! Peter and Sara are standing there waiting.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.fi: Hej Sara! Hej Peter! Hur är det?
lines.en: Hi Sara! Hi Peter! How are you?

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.fi: Det är okej men vi väntade så länge på er... Ni är mycket sena! Filmen börjar om 5 minuter!
lines.en: It is okay, but we waited so long for you. You are very late! The film starts in five minutes!

listenQuestions.prompt: Who is waiting for Ingrid and Sofia?

naturalNotes.note: Write dem for the object form. In Sweden de and dem both usually sound like dom, as the app’s voices say them. In Finland many people still say de (often like di) and dem differently.

hunt.title: Find the marked forms.

spots.rule: me (jag → mig). Hör du mig? Said mej.
you, one person (du → dig). Skynda dig! = Hurry up! Said dej.
us (vi → oss), after på: väntar på oss.
him (han → honom), after för: berätta för honom.
her (hon → henne): ringa henne. Not hennes, which means her as owner.
them (de → dem): Jag ser dem. Often said dom.

listenQuestions.explanation: Tolv is 12; tolfte is 12th. The v becomes f.
Åttonde is eighth. Arton is eighteen.

naturalNotes.natural: den första, den andra, den tredje, den tjugofjärde
naturalNotes.note: Write :a after 1, 2, 21, 22 and 31, because första and andra end in -a. All others take :e. Letters often write just den 24 maj.
From 21 to 31, join the tens and the order word: tjugo + första, trettio + första.
The app’s Sweden-Swedish voices melt r into the next sound (första sounds like “fösh-ta”). In Finland the r is usually said on its own.

hunt.label: Ordinal hunt
hunt.title: Find the order words that need care.
hunt.instructions: Tap the ordinals that do not simply add -nde. The note explains each trap.
hunt.missHint: Look in the line from första to tionde, and at elfte and tolfte.

spots.rule: 1st. Its own word, not from ett. Written 1:a.
2nd. Its own word, not from två. Written 2:a.
3rd, from tre. Written 3:e, like all the rest.
4th, from fyra. The vowel changes: fyr → fjär.
5th, from fem: add -te, not -nde. Written 5:e.
6th, from sex. Said with the sj-sound (in Finland often close to English sh).
8th, from åtta. The page marks the o: åttOnde. Do not mix it up with arton (18).
11th, from elva. The v becomes f: elFte.
12th, from tolv. The v becomes f: tolFte.

homework.title: Definite plural of nouns
homework.instructions: Skriv substantivet i bestämd form plural. Choose or write the plural with “the”: plurals that end in -r get -na (bilar → bilarna, veckor → veckorna, bananer → bananerna), plurals ending in -n get -a (möten → mötena), and ett-words with no plural ending get -en (hus → husen).

questions.prompt: Anita ska ha en fest. Hon gick till en butik och vill köpa kläder. _______ i butiken är mycket dyra. (KLÄNNING)
questions.translation: Anita is going to have a party. She went to a shop and wants to buy clothes. ___ in the shop are very expensive. (dress)

questions.prompt: Ahmed vill laga mat. Han är på Lidl och köper ingredienser. ______ är söta så han tänker laga tårta. (JORDGUBBE)
questions.translation: Ahmed wants to cook. He is at Lidl buying ingredients. ___ are sweet, so he is planning to make a cake. (strawberry)

questions.prompt: Yasmin vill baka bananbröd. ______ på Lidl är ganska gröna så hon måste gå till en annan affär. (BANAN)
questions.translation: Yasmin wants to bake banana bread. ___ at Lidl are quite green, so she has to go to another shop. (banana)

questions.prompt: Ola och Ulla vill flytta till landet. _____ i stan är för dyra. (HUS)
questions.translation: Ola and Ulla want to move to the countryside. ___ in town are too expensive. (house)

questions.prompt: Vi har så mycket att göra på jobbet så vi hade många möten. _____ är ganska tråkiga. (MÖTE)
questions.translation: We have so much to do at work, so we had a lot of meetings. ___ are quite boring. (meeting)

questions.prompt: Usama har två bilar hemma. _____ är tyska och svarta.
questions.translation: Usama has two cars at home. ___ are German and black.
questions.hint: Write the noun in the definite plural (the …s).

questions.prompt: Mira köpte många väskor. ______ var inte billiga.
questions.translation: Mira bought a lot of bags. ___ were not cheap.
questions.hint: Write the noun in the definite plural (the …s).

questions.prompt: Restaurangen "Lyx" är mycket populär och har många kunder på kvällen. _____ beställer ofta laxsoppan och kötbullarna.
questions.translation: The restaurant "Lyx" is very popular and has a lot of customers in the evening. ___ often order the salmon soup and the meatballs.

Barn: Mamma, min äppeljuice är grön!
Mamma: Ja, den är gjord av äpplen. Och _____ var gröna!

questions.hint: Write the noun in the definite plural (the …s).

homework.title: Objektspronomen
homework.instructions: Välj subjektspronomen eller objektspronomen. The subject form (jag, du, han, hon, vi, ni) is the person who does the action. The object form (mig, dig, honom, henne, oss, er) receives the action or comes after a preposition such as med, till, för, på.

sections.title: The specific things and people
body: Swedish puts “the” on the end: bilen (the car), bilarna (the cars). Hindi and Marathi have no “the”, so this ending is easy to forget.
Start from the plural (Lecture 7) and look at its last letter: -r → add -na (bilarna), -n → add -a (mötena), no ending → add -en (barnen).
Exception: words in -are, such as lärare and hamburgare, drop the e and add -na: lärarna, hamburgarna.
Use it for specific ones: Pojkarna som jag känner (the boys I know). For things in general, no ending: Många pojkar gillar bilar. Båda (both) takes it: båda bilarna.
Typical mistake: -arna on every word. It is bananerna, because the plural is bananer.

examples.fi: Mötena är långa, men jobben är roliga.
examples.en: The meetings are long, but the jobs are fun.

examples.fi: Jag köpte en bil. Bilen är tysk. Nu har jag två bilar. Båda bilarna är tyska.
examples.en: I bought a car. The car is German. Now I have two cars. Both cars are German.
examples.note: en bil → bilen → bilar → bilarna (teacher’s example)

examples.fi: Ingen gillar stränga lärare. Lärarna på vår skola är inte stränga.
examples.en: Nobody likes strict teachers. The teachers at our school are not strict.
examples.note: General first, then specific. Vår = our.

examples.fi: Jag känner lärarna, men jag vet inte vad de heter.
examples.en: I know the teachers, but I do not know their names.
examples.note: känner = know a person; vet = know a fact

sections.memoryTip: Look at the plural’s last letter: -r → -na, -n → -a, nothing → -en.
sections.tryIt: Say “the tickets, the apples, the children, the bananas”: biljetterna, äpplena, barnen, bananerna.

activity.label: Choose the ending
activity.title: Which ending makes the “the” plural?
activity.instructions: Each card shows a plural. Look at its last letter and choose the ending that makes “the” plural. One card is the exception.

items.why: Ends in -r: veckor + na = veckorna.
Ends in -r: biljetter + na = biljetterna.
Ends in -r: bananerna, not bananarna.
Ends in -r: nycklar + na = nycklarna.
Ends in -n: möten + a = mötena.
Ends in -n: äpplen + a = äpplena.
No plural ending: barn + en = barnen.
No plural ending: jobb + en = jobben.
The exception: a person word in -are drops its last e and adds -na: lärarna.

activity.summary: Say each “the” form aloud: veckorna, biljetterna, bananerna, nycklarna, mötena, äpplena, barnen, jobben, lärarna.

sections.title: Who receives the action?
body: The subject does the action; the object receives it: Elin ringer mig. After på, med, för, till or från, use the object form too: Vänta på mig!
Decide by role, not place. In a yes/no question or after a time word, the doer comes after the verb (Lecture 3) but keeps its form: Kan du hjälpa mig? I dag kan jag inte.
Hindi main → mujhe and Marathi mī → malā work like jag → mig. But “I like” is mujhe pasand hai or malā āvaḍta, while Swedish says Jag gillar, never Mig gillar.
Swedish splits English you: dig for one person, er for several. Henne is her; hennes is her as owner (hennes bil).
De or dem? Both often sound like dom. Where vi would fit, write de; where oss would fit, write dem.
Skynda dig! (Hurry up!) changes with the person: Skynda er! Vi måste skynda oss. De måste skynda sig, not dem (a slip in the teacher’s note).

examples.fi: Jag kan hjälpa dig. Kan du hjälpa mig?
examples.en: I can help you. Can you help me?
examples.note: dig and mig receive the action.

examples.fi: Vänta på mig! Prata med dem!
examples.en: Wait for me! Talk with them!
examples.note: Object forms after på and med (teacher’s examples).

examples.fi: Jag såg henne i går. Jag fick en present från er.
examples.en: I saw her yesterday. I got a present from you (all).
examples.note: henne after a verb; er after från.

examples.fi: Berätta allt för mig! Jag ska laga mat till oss.
examples.en: Tell me everything! I will cook for us.
examples.note: berätta för + person; till oss = for us

examples.fi: Lämna inte utan mig! Jag vill inte vänta på honom.
examples.en: Do not leave without me! I do not want to wait for him.
examples.note: Object forms after utan and på (teacher’s examples).

sections.memoryTip: Ask who does it and who receives it. The place in the sentence does not decide.
sections.tryIt: Say Jag ringer Elin, then Jag ringer henne. Then ask: Kan du hjälpa mig?

activity.label: Swap the name
activity.title: Replace the names with a pronoun
activity.instructions: Read each sentence with names. Find the same sentence with an object pronoun, then say it aloud.

pairs.left: Jag väntar på dig och Mikko.

activity.pattern: Who receives it? one woman → henne, one man → honom, you and others → er, others → dem, me and others → oss.

activities.label: Doer or receiver?
activities.title: Which form fills the gap?
activities.instructions: Does the missing word do the action or receive it? Choose, then say the whole sentence.

items.why: jag: after i dag the verb comes second, then the doer (Lecture 3).
mig: Elin calls; you receive the call.
Jag: Swedish uses the doer, unlike mujhe pasand hai or malā āvaḍta.

items.en: Do you know where the cinema is?
items.why: du: you do the knowing, even after the verb.

items.en: We are waiting for you (one person).
items.why: dig: object form after på.

items.en: Maja is sending the tickets to us.
items.why: oss: object form after till.

items.fi: Där står Alex och Maja. Ser du ___?
items.en: Alex and Maja are standing there. Do you see them?
items.why: dem: you see them. Write dem even when you hear dom.

buckets.label: Doer form
buckets.hint: jag, du, han, hon, vi, ni, de

buckets.label: Receiver form
buckets.hint: mig, dig, honom, henne, oss, er, dem

activities.summary: The role decides, not the place: in Kan du hjälpa mig? du comes after the verb but still helps.

sections.title: Order numbers and dates
body: A date is den + ordinal + month: den tredje juni. The months are almost English, with a small letter (see the table).
Lecture 10 gave första, andra, tredje. Learn up to tolfte by heart. From 13th most add -nde (trettonde); from 21st, join the parts (tjugoförsta).
Traps: åttonde (8th) but arton (18); elva, tolv → elfte, tolfte; fem → femte.
Written: den 24 maj or den 24:e maj (:a after 1, 2, 21, 22, 31). Finnish notices write 24.5., day first. You may also hear den tjugofjärde i femte (“the 24th of the 5th”).
Birthdays: När fyller du år? Jag fyller år den tionde maj.

examples.fi: Jag fyller år den tionde maj.
examples.en: My birthday is on the tenth of May.
examples.note: fylla år = have a birthday (teacher’s example)

examples.fi: Jag föddes den åttonde oktober. Min födelsedag är den åttonde oktober.
examples.en: I was born on the eighth of October. My birthday is on the eighth of October.
examples.note: föddes = was born; three ways to give your birthday (teacher’s examples)

examples.fi: Jag ordnar en fest den trettionde september.
examples.en: I am having a party on the thirtieth of September.
examples.note: Written den 30 september or den 30:e september (teacher’s example)

examples.fi: Alex fyller år den tjugoåttonde maj. Festen är på lördag den trettionde.
examples.en: Alex’s birthday is on the twenty-eighth of May. The party is on Saturday the thirtieth.
examples.note: tjugo + åttonde; weekday first, then den + date

examples.en: Independence Day is on the sixth of December.

examples.fi: – Vilket datum är det i dag? – Det är den trettonde maj.
examples.en: – What is the date today? – It is the thirteenth of May.

sections.memoryTip: 24.5. → den tjugofjärde maj: day first, then den + ordinal + month.
sections.tryIt: Say today’s date. Then say your birthday: Jag fyller år den …

activity.label: Read Finnish dates
activity.title: Say the dates you see on Finnish notices
activity.instructions: Finnish short dates put the day first. Match each to what you say. Watch 6.12. and 12.6., and 8th and 18th.
activity.pattern: Day first, then month: 6.12. = den sjätte december.

sections.title: Invite, answer and suggest
body: Invite: Vill du gå på bio med mig? or simply Vill du följa med? (Do you want to come along?)
Accept: Ja, gärna! Det låter kul! Det passar mig bra.
Say no in three parts: thanks or sorry, a short reason, a new idea. Tack för inbjudan! Tyvärr kan jag inte då, jag ska jobba. Kan vi gå på lördag i stället? A bare Nej sounds cold.
Close the plan: date, time and place, then check: Passar det dig?

assignment.title: Lecture 11 mission: A cinema invitation
assignment.instructions:
CORE: Invite someone to the cinema. Agree on a date, time and meeting place, use an object pronoun, and offer a second date with i stället.

WRITE: Send a YKI-style message: say sorry, say why you cannot come, and suggest another day with a date.

RETURN: Repeat the invitation from memory with a changed date.
assignment.model: Vill du gå på bio med mig på söndag den tjugofjärde maj? Vi träffas framför bion kvart i sju. Passar det dig? Annars kan vi gå den tjugotredje i stället.

takeaways: For “the” in plural, look at the plural’s last letter: -r → -na, -n → -a, nothing → -en (lärare → lärarna).
Choose the pronoun by role, not place: the doer is jag, du, han …; the receiver, also after på, med or till, is mig, dig, honom … Kan du hjälpa mig?
A date is den + ordinal + month: den tjugofjärde maj, written 24.5. on Finnish notices. Watch åttonde (8th) and arton (18).
A kind no has thanks or sorry, a reason and a new idea: Tyvärr kan jag inte då. Kan vi gå på lördag i stället?
